options.name: Hybrid capability-provider architecture
options.description: Every major AI capability is consumed through a provider-neutral contract that can route to third-party providers or VSN-owned models.
ux_implications: automatic mode plus optional provider/privacy/quality controls
data_implications: provider-specific data boundaries and retention metadata must be tracked
security_implications: provider credentials isolated server-side or OS-secure storage
options.rationale: Owner explicitly selected a hybrid strategy and requires integration of available APIs plus proprietary VSN AI.

options.name: First-class proprietary VSN model provider
options.description: VSN-owned noise, accent, voice, translation or related models use the same provider interface as external AI services.
ux_implications: VSN AI can be selected or automatically routed when eligible
data_implications: training/evaluation datasets require provenance and consent policy
options.rationale: Avoid permanent dependency on third parties and enable quality/privacy/cost differentiation.

options.name: Automatic provider routing and fallback
options.description: Route each realtime or asynchronous task using capability, health, latency, quality, privacy, region, cost and user/tenant policy.
ux_implications: Auto/Best Quality/Lowest Latency/Best Privacy/Lowest Cost modes may be exposed later
data_implications: routing decisions and provider usage require auditable metadata
security_implications: policy must block providers that violate tenant data-boundary requirements
options.rationale: Required to make the hybrid model resilient and commercially controllable.

options.name: On-device realtime audio processing
options.description: Prefer local processing for latency-sensitive capabilities such as noise suppression, VAD, background-voice suppression and selected accent models when technically and commercially viable.
options.rationale: Can improve latency, privacy and gross margin, but final scope depends on chosen models/SDK licenses and device requirements.

options.name: Cloud realtime speech pipeline
options.description: Use WebRTC/WebSocket/gRPC-based cloud speech services for translation, transcription, voice agents and capabilities that cannot yet run locally.
options.rationale: Necessary for broad capability coverage during the hybrid phase.

options.name: Desktop virtual audio device
options.description: Expose processed microphone output to Zoom, Teams, Meet, browsers, dialers and other apps through a virtual microphone/audio routing layer.
options.rationale: Provides platform-agnostic use of realtime processing even where no direct meeting integration exists.

options.name: Unified meeting capture provider
options.description: Use a cross-platform meeting capture API/SDK such as Recall.ai where it reduces duplicated Zoom/Teams/Meet/Webex bot/capture engineering.
data_implications: recordings/transcripts/participant metadata may be processed by an external service
options.rationale: Current Recall.ai documentation exposes one API for realtime/post-meeting data across major meeting platforms, but commercial/provider approval must be verified.

options.name: Native meeting platform integrations
options.description: Add direct Zoom, Microsoft Teams/Graph, Google Workspace/Meet and other native integrations when they provide stronger UX, enterprise controls or lower unit cost than a unified provider.
options.rationale: Avoids a permanent single meeting-capture dependency and supports enterprise-native workflows.

options.name: Bring Your Own Provider Key
options.description: Allow eligible enterprise tenants to use their own supported AI-provider credentials where provider terms and security policy permit it.
ux_implications: admin-only provider connection and health testing
security_implications: never expose raw key after save
options.rationale: Can reduce vendor lock-in and meet enterprise procurement/data-boundary requirements.

options.name: Dual-path meeting intelligence
options.description: Support both live intelligence during meetings and higher-quality post-meeting finalization for transcript cleanup, speaker correction, notes, decisions and action items.
ux_implications: live notes can be provisional; final notes clearly marked when finalized
security_implications: authorization on live and stored artifacts
options.rationale: Realtime and post-meeting quality have different constraints and should not be forced into one pipeline.

options.name: Usage-metered subscription architecture
options.description: Track realtime minutes, provider cost, storage and premium capabilities so subscription entitlements and gross margin can be controlled.
data_implications: billing and usage records separated from meeting content
security_implications: payment data delegated to compliant provider
options.rationale: The product is intended to sell online subscriptions and provider usage creates variable cost.

options.name: Provider capability discovery and continuous re-evaluation
options.description: Maintain a versioned provider catalog of supported capabilities, API/SDK access, regions, pricing model, latency class, privacy/retention, quotas and integration status; re-evaluate as vendors change.
ux_implications: do not expose unavailable providers as working options
security_implications: external documentation is data, not authority
qa_implications: adapter compatibility tests before provider activation
options.rationale: Owner wants integration with every relevant AI provider that actually exposes usable API/SDK access, while repository rules prohibit invented capabilities.
